h1: The 7 Best Aluminum Portable Wheelchair Ramps for Steps and Thresholds, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 aluminum portable wheelchair ramps from 2 to 12 feet, compared on rise range, capacity, weight, folded size and slope safety.
summary: The TaiH Leo 8FT ramp with support legs is the best portable aluminum ramp for porches, and folding in half and covering rises of 8 to 24 inches. The HYUNAN METHOD 4FT is the best compact ramp, with guardrails, an 800 pound capacity and an 18.43 pound weight, and the FACHNUO 12FT handles tall porches and van floors.
intro: The number that matters most on a wheelchair ramp is not on the front of the box. It is the ratio of length to rise. A ramp that climbs one inch for every twelve inches of length, called a 1:12 slope, is the commonly cited guideline for independent wheelchair use. Many portable ramps list rise ranges that push well past it, and a short ramp on a tall step is a steep ramp, whatever the listing says.

We reviewed seven aluminum portable ramps from 2 to 12 feet and ranked them on length, rise range, capacity, weight and folded size. We treat the top of every listed rise range with caution: use a longer ramp when a person is propelling themselves, and use a helper when you cannot. Always confirm with the user's clinician or the ramp maker for your exact chair, rise and abilities.

products.name: TaiH Leo 8FT Wheelchair Ramp With Support Legs
products.verdict: An 8 foot ramp that halves for carrying and rides on adjustable support legs.
products.description:
The TaiH Leo is an 8 foot aluminum ramp that halves in length when folded, with a platform about 29 inches wide and adjustable support legs. The maker lists it for rises of 8 to 24 inches. It costs $200 to $500.

It wins because 8 feet gives a gentler slope than the short ramps on porch steps, and the support legs hold the middle of the ramp so it does not flex under a chair. At 8 feet, a rise of 8 inches is close to the 1:12 guideline, which is the sweet spot. For higher rises, the upper end of the range gets steep.

Buy it for a porch or step of roughly 8 inches. Longer rises need a longer ramp or a helper.
pros: 8 foot length gives a gentler slope
products.idealFor: Porches and steps with a rise near 8 inches.
products.skipIf: You only need a short threshold ramp.

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 4FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: A 4 foot ramp with guardrails, reflective strips and an 800 pound capacity.
products.description:
The HYUNAN METHOD ramp is 4 feet long, weighs 18.43 pounds and holds 800 pounds. The surface is about 29 inches wide, it folds in half for carrying, and it comes with guardrails and reflective strips. It costs $100 to $200.

It takes second place because guardrails and reflective strips are safety features that many portable ramps lack, and the weight is manageable for one person to carry. The listing says it fits 4 to 12 inch rises, but a 4 foot ramp suits about a 4 inch rise on the 1:12 guideline, so a taller step needs a helper or a longer ramp.

Buy it for one or two low steps. Do not use it on a rise much above 4 inches without assistance.
products.idealFor: Homes with one or two low steps.
products.skipIf: Your step is taller than about 6 inches.

products.name: FACHNUO 12FT Wheelchair Ramp With Support Legs
products.verdict: A 12 foot ramp for tall porches and van floors, with support legs.
products.description:
The FACHNUO 12FT ramp runs 12 feet when open and six feet when folded, with a 29 inch wide surface and support legs. It is listed for rises of 12 to 36 inches and costs $500 and up.

It ranks third because length is the real solution for a tall step. At 12 feet the ramp can safely cover a rise near 12 inches on the 1:12 guideline, and the long span with legs resists sagging. The tradeoff is storage, since even folded it is 6 feet long, and carrying it is a two-person job.

Buy it for a tall porch or vehicle entry where nothing shorter would be safe. Check your storage space first.

products.name: VNN Portable Wheelchair Ramp 6FT Seamless
products.verdict: A 6 foot ramp with a seamless center hinge and a double non-skid surface.
products.description:
The VNN 6FT ramp has a seamless center hinge, a double non-skid surface and folds for carrying. It fits rises of 6 to 18 inches and costs $200 to $500.

The seamless hinge matters because the gap at a standard center hinge is a bump for small caster wheels. A double non-skid surface adds grip in wet weather. At 6 feet, it suits a rise of about 6 inches on the 1:12 guideline, so the 18 inch upper range needs a helper. It sits fourth because it lacks support legs and guardrail details.

Buy it for a moderate step with a smooth ride. Check the folded size on the retailer page.
products.idealFor: Moderate steps where a smooth ride matters.
products.skipIf: Your rise is above about 8 inches.

products.name: KOLOTOOL Portable Wheelchair Ramp 3FT
products.verdict: A 3 foot, 800 pound ramp that folds in half for one or two steps.
products.description:
The KOLOTOOL 3FT ramp folds in half and holds 800 pounds, with a listed fit for rises of 3 to 9 inches and one or two steps. It costs $100 to $200.

A 3 foot ramp suits a rise of about 3 inches on the 1:12 guideline, which is a single low step. It ranks fifth because it covers that job well and stows in a closet, but the 9 inch upper limit is far steeper than comfortable. It is a good ramp for the right step and a poor one for the wrong step.

Buy it for a single low step or a door threshold. Do not trust the top of its rise range.
cons: Very steep at the upper range
products.idealFor: A single low step or door threshold.
products.skipIf: Your step is above about 4 inches.

products.name: FACHNUO 2FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: A 10.9 pound, 2 foot ramp with baffles and reflective strips for door sills.
products.description:
The FACHNUO 2FT ramp is two feet long, about 29 inches wide and weighs 10.9 pounds, with baffles and reflective strips for traction and visibility. It costs $50 to $100.

A 2 foot ramp matches a rise of about 2 inches on the 1:12 guideline, so it is for door sills and very low single steps. It places sixth because of the narrow range of use. Its low weight and small folded size make it easy to carry in a car trunk or bag.

Buy it for door thresholds and a very low curb. It is not suited to porch steps.

products.name: VNN Portable Wheelchair Ramp 4FT
products.verdict: A basic 4 foot folding ramp from a line that offers longer sizes.
products.description:
The VNN 4FT ramp folds for carrying, has a folded aluminum surface with a non-skid layer and is listed for 4 to 12 inch steps. It costs $100 to $200, and the line offers longer sizes.

It ranks last because it is the plainest, with no capacity, weight or guardrails listed. The 4 foot length suits a rise near 4 inches on the 1:12 guideline, and the 12 inch top of its range would be very steep. The line's longer sizes are a plus if your needs grow.

Buy it as a basic ramp with room to upgrade within the line. Check the capacity before use.
products.idealFor: Basic use, with an option to upsize.
products.skipIf: You need guardrails or stated capacity.

methodology.description: We judged each ramp against the 1:12 slope guideline, treating rise ranges that exceed it as needing a helper or a longer ramp.

whatMatters.detail: The commonly cited guideline is one inch of rise per twelve inches of ramp, called 1:12. A 4 inch step therefore wants a 4 foot ramp, and a 12 inch step wants 12 feet. Measure the vertical rise from ground to the top of the step and choose a length that respects the ratio.
Capacity must cover the user, the chair and any scooter or equipment. An 800 pound rating gives a good safety margin. If the listing states no capacity, ask the maker before use.
A non-skid surface keeps wheels and shoes from slipping, particularly when wet. Edge guards or guardrails help stop wheels leaving the side. Reflective strips make the ramp visible at night.
Long ramps can flex in the middle under weight, and support legs hold the span in place. Adjustable legs help on uneven ground. Look for them on ramps of 8 feet or more.
A lighter ramp is easier to carry and stow, but a long ramp stays bulky. Compare the folded size to your car trunk or storage space. Check that the carry handle is comfortable.

howToChoose.intro: Measure the rise first, then choose a ramp whose length respects the 1:12 guideline.

howToChoose.subheading: Short Folding Ramp vs Long Ramp With Legs

cards.label: Short folding ramp
cards.text: Light, easy to carry and good for low steps and thresholds. The KOLOTOOL 3FT, HYUNAN METHOD 4FT and FACHNUO 2FT are examples.

cards.label: Long ramp with legs
cards.text: A gentler slope for porches and tall steps, with legs to stop flex. The TaiH Leo 8FT and FACHNUO 12FT work this way.

howToChoose.note: Choose a short ramp only for steps of about 4 inches or less, and go longer for anything higher.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A length that matches the rise at 1:12, support legs, a non-skid surface and a width of around 29 inches. Anchor or place the ramp so it cannot slide.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The TaiH Leo 8FT is the best porch ramp, and the FACHNUO 12FT is the choice for taller porches. Discuss installation with a qualified professional.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The rise is more than a few inches or the ramp is for daily use. The TaiH Leo and FACHNUO 12FT at $200 and up give safer slopes.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only cross a low threshold. The FACHNUO 2FT at $50 to $100 is enough.

faq.q: How do I measure the rise?
faq.a: Measure the vertical height from the ground to the top of the step or threshold. Divide by one inch per foot of ramp to find the minimum length. When in doubt, choose a longer ramp.

faq.q: What is the common mistake buying a ramp?
faq.a: Trusting the listed rise range. Many ramps list ranges that would be very steep for a self-propelling user. Use the 1:12 guideline or ask a clinician.

faq.q: Is a portable ramp worth it over a permanent one?
faq.a: For occasional use, travel or rentals, yes. A permanent ramp is safer for daily use at home. Portable ramps are not a substitute for a properly installed home ramp.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Unfold on a flat surface, extend the legs if fitted and place it so the top rests on the step with no gap. Check that it does not slide. Test it with an assistant.

faq.q: How do I keep it safe in rain and ice?
faq.a: Keep the non-skid surface clean and clear snow and ice. Dry it before use. Do not use a wet ramp on a steep slope.

faq.q: Can a ramp be used with a mobility scooter?
faq.a: Check the capacity and width against the scooter and rider. The 800 pound models have room, but confirm the scooter's weight. Ask the maker if unsure.

finalTake: The TaiH Leo 8FT is the best portable aluminum ramp for porches, because its length and support legs give a safer slope. The HYUNAN METHOD 4FT is the best compact ramp with guardrails and an 800 pound capacity, and the FACHNUO 12FT is the choice for tall porches or van floors. Always match the ramp length to the rise rather than trusting the listed range, and ask a clinician when in doubt.
